title: Reclaiming Boundaries: From Enmeshment to Self
summary: A comprehensive seven-module program designed to help you untangle your sense of self from the needs of others. Using CBT and assertiveness training, you will learn to recognize the 'fawn' response, set guilt-free boundaries, and build relationships based on healthy interdependence rather than fearful enmeshment.

modules.title: Module 1 • Diagnosis of the 'Nice'
modules.overview: We redefine codependency not as 'loving too much' but as a fear response (fawning). It is a strategy to stay safe. We identify the 'Resentmentometer.' If you feel resentful, it means you said 'yes' when you meant 'no.' Psycho-education on the 'Chameleon Effect'—changing your colors to fit the room. We introduce the concept of 'Emotional Fusion.' Feeling responsible for other people's feelings.
takeaways: Codependency is a loss of self in the service of safety.
Resentment is the primary symptom of a boundary violation.
You are not responsible for regulating other people's emotions.
exercises: The Resentment Log: Track moments of resentment this week. What did you agree to? What did you actually want?
The 'Yes' Audit: For every 'Yes' you say this week, ask yourself: 'Did I say yes out of desire or out of fear?'
homework: Write a definition of who you are *outside* of your roles (mother, partner, employee).

modules.title: Module 2 • The Architecture of Boundaries
modules.overview: What is a boundary? It is not a wall; it is a gate. You have the key. We distinguish between Porous, Rigid, and Healthy boundaries. We identify your 'Property Line.' What falls inside your yard (your feelings, your body, your time) vs. their yard (their feelings, their choices). Cognitive Restructuring for 'Selfishness.' Reframing self-care as self-preservation.
takeaways: Boundaries define where you end and the other person begins.
Rigid boundaries keep love out; porous boundaries let harm in.
Saying no to them is saying yes to you.
exercises: The Fence Visualization: Draw your property line. List what is inside (My mood, my money) and outside (Mom's mood, Partner's addiction).
The 'Not My Job' List: Write a list of things you are currently managing that are actually other people's responsibilities.
homework: Identify one item from the 'Not My Job' list and stop doing it.
Practice saying 'I need to think about that' instead of an immediate 'Yes'.

modules.title: Module 3 • Tolerating the Guilt Gap
modules.overview: Setting a boundary triggers guilt. This module teaches you to tolerate that guilt without collapsing. We distinguish 'Clean Guilt' (I hurt someone) from 'False Guilt' (I disappointed someone). Exposure therapy for saying 'No.' We treat the discomfort of saying no as something to be felt, not fixed. The 'Guilt Gap' concept: The time between setting the boundary and the guilt fading.
takeaways: Guilt is the price of admission for a free life.
Just because you feel guilty doesn't mean you did something wrong.
Others' disappointment is not your danger.
exercises: The Guilt Delay: When you feel guilty, wait 10 minutes before apologizing or fixing it. Often the feeling passes.
Reframing: Replace 'I feel guilty' with 'I feel uncomfortable because I am doing something new.'
homework: Set one small boundary that provokes mild guilt. Sit with the feeling for 30 minutes without fixing it.

modules.title: Module 4 • Assertive Communication
modules.overview: Moving from Passive (doormat) or Passive-Aggressive (hinting) to Assertive. The 'DEAR MAN' script from DBT adapted for boundaries. Learning to say 'No' without over-explaining. 'No' is a complete sentence. Handling pushback. When they say 'You've changed,' how to respond.
takeaways: Over-explaining is a trauma response; keep it simple.
Assertiveness is kind; clear is kind.
You can be firm and loving at the same time.
exercises: Script Writing: Write a script for a boundary you need to set. Remove all JADE-ing.
The Broken Record: Practice repeating your boundary ('I'm not able to help') without adding new excuses.
homework: Deliver your script to the person (or a low-stakes person first).

modules.title: Module 5 • Detaching with Love
modules.overview: How to love someone without being enmeshed. Specifically for relationships with addicts or high-conflict people. The concept of 'Detachment.' You can care about them without carrying them. Stopping the 'Rescue.' Why saving them actually prevents their growth. Focusing back on your own life.
takeaways: You cannot save people from their own karma.
Detachment is not abandonment; it is allowing them the dignity of their own consequences.
Your stability is the best thing you can offer them.
exercises: The Rescue Audit: List ways you are rescuing someone (giving money, lying for them, listening to the same complaint). Stop one.
The 'My Life' Pie Chart: Draw a chart of your mental energy. How much is about them? How much is about you? Redraw it how you want it.
homework: Practice one act of detachment (e.g., not offering advice when they complain).
Spend that energy on a hobby for yourself.

modules.title: Module 6 • Knowing Your Needs
modules.overview: Codependents are experts on others' needs and strangers to their own. Reconnecting with the body. What do *I* want to eat? Where do *I* want to go? Validating your own reality. Trusting your gut. Asking for what you want directly.
takeaways: You have needs, and they are valid.
It is your job to express your needs, not their job to guess them.
Self-trust is the antidote to codependency.
exercises: The Preference Practice: Make 3 trivial decisions today based solely on what you want (coffee vs tea, walk vs sit).
The Direct Ask: Ask for one thing from a partner or friend. 'Could you please take out the trash?' No hinting.
homework: Go on a 'date' with yourself to a place you want to go, just because you want to.

modules.title: Module 7 • Interdependence: The Goal
modules.overview: We are not aiming for isolation; we are aiming for healthy interdependence. What a healthy relationship looks like: Two whole people, not two halves. Reciprocity check. Are you giving and receiving? Maintaining boundaries while deepening intimacy.
takeaways: Dependency is 'I need you to survive.' Interdependence is 'I can survive alone, but I choose you.'
Vulnerability requires boundaries.
You are safe to be yourself.
exercises: Relationship Inventory: Evaluate your core relationships. Which are interdependent? Which are codependent?
The Vow to Self: Write a vow to never abandon yourself again.
homework: Share your new definition of the relationship with a safe person.
Celebrate your graduation from the school of people-pleasing.

aiSupport.systemPrompt: Help the user apply one concrete module step at a time. Do not diagnose. Escalate urgent safety concerns to emergency care.
